newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares fall back from highs at mid-session.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares fall back from highs at mid-session.

text.p: Delhi shares retreated from early peaks in mid-session trade on Thursday, falling back through psychological barrier as speculators pocketed profits, brokers said.

The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index was 6.42 points higher at 783.44 at 1:00 p.m. (0730 GMT). After 30 minutes of trade, the index had gained four percent, piercing the 800-point barrier to 802.10.

"A slowdown in buying by foreign investors and speculators at higher levels followed by a revival of heavy selling by profit takers put a break on the rise in share prices," said Anil Saigal of brokers A.K. Saigal.
The early rise was fuelled by a report in the Economic Times that Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda would announce a major economic package within a week to boost the capital market.

A Finance Ministry official who asked not to be identified said "a few initiatives are in the pipeline and can be expected over the next week or so". The official declined to say whether there would be a major economic package.
Last month Deve Gowda promised to take steps this month to boost capital markets and attract more private investment into key industrial sectors.
Reliance Industries, after touching a high of 270 rupees in early trade, was 7.80 rupees higher at 259, brokers said.
State Bank of India gained 7.40 rupees to 297.
